topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's themes and outlines the learning objectives for cancer genetics.

topics.label: Tumor viruses, cellular oncogenes, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the study of transforming viruses revealed cellular oncogenes and established laboratory assays for measuring oncogenic transformation.

topics.label: Oncogenes, tumor suppressors, and mutational mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the definitions, regulatory pathways, and molecular mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how failures in DNA replication, repair pathways, and mitotic chromosome segregation generate sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the stepwise accumulation of somatic and inherited mutations drives tumor development and evolution.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session, offers to answer questions, and recommends supplementary reading.
